note: The fuzzer allocates a NUL-terminated copy of the raw SSML input.
The candidate bytes <<foo are copied unchanged into the synthesized string.

code: espeak_Synth((char*) str, size + 1, 0, POS_CHARACTER, 0, synth_flags, NULL, NULL);
note: The call enables espeakSSML, so ReadClause treats angle-bracket input as SSML markup.
The first byte is a literal '<', entering SSML tag handling.
The second input byte is another '<', so the first branch is skipped without consuming it as text; the loop advances and then treats foo as a tag after the second '<'.
The malformed tag has no closing '>', so the loop copies foo and exits only when the decoder reaches EOF.
The final in-loop GetC reaches the byte after the input string, making Eof true.
After processing the unterminated tag, the code unconditionally reads another character even though Eof is already true, causing the ASan stack-buffer-overflow read.
